datasets.instrument_sensor: Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer (MEDA) instrument package; specifically Relative Humidity Sensor (HS) and Thermal Infrared Sensor (TIRS) (also ATS air temperature mentioned)
datasets.measurement_observable: Relative humidity; atmospheric pressure; air temperature; ground brightness temperature; derived water vapor volume mixing ratio (VMR); derived surface water activity (aw)
datasets.wavelength_bandpass: TIRS surface brightness temperature in the 8–14 µm range
datasets.data_type_product_type: In-situ environmental time-series measurements; derived parameters (VMR, aw)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: First Martian year of Perseverance surface operations; examples include sols 285–305 (Ls=139°–149°) and analyses over one full Martian year; sealing times for samples span LMST ~16:25 to 22:16 (Table 1)
datasets.location_coverage: Jezero crater, Mars; landing site given as [18.4663°N, 77.4298°E]; sensor heights referenced at 1.45 m (HS) and ~0.84 m (sealing-station height/ATS); TIRS footprint is a downward-looking ellipsoid area of ~3–4 m²
datasets.spatial_resolution: TIRS footprint covering an ellipsoid area of 3–4 m²
datasets.temporal_resolution_cadence: HS output stated reliable for local times ~20:00–07:00; ATS plotted with 300 s moving average (measurement cadence otherwise referenced to Supporting Information A)
datasets.how_used: Used MEDA HS (RH) and pressure to retrieve near-surface H2O vapor pressure and VMR, and MEDA TIRS ground temperature to compute surface water activity aw over a full Martian year at Jezero; MEDA pressure/temperature at ~0.84 m used to estimate headspace gas moles and H2O partial pressure at sample sealing times; MEDA data compared with TES orbital water column climatology and used to validate/drive single-column model (SCM) fits.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Thermal Emission Spectrometer (TES) derived water column abundance climatology dataset (non-normalized to constant surface pressure)
datasets.measurement_observable: Total column H2O abundance / water vapor column abundance (precipitable microns)
datasets.data_type_product_type: Orbital gridded climatology dataset (column abundance in latitude/longitude/Ls bins; zonally averaged)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Mars Years 24–27; daytime observations with LMST ~14:00; Ls in 5° averaged bins
datasets.location_coverage: Latitudinal bin encompassing Jezero crater: 18°–21°N latitude; data provided in 3° latitude and 7.5° longitude bins; values zonally averaged (Fig. 2 Bottom)
datasets.temporal_resolution_cadence: Seasonal bins of Ls=5°; daytime LMST ~14:00
datasets.how_used: Used TES zonally-averaged daytime orbital water vapor column abundances for the Jezero latitude band (MY24–MY27) to compare against MEDA-derived nighttime precipitable water estimates and assess seasonal coherence and magnitude differences (factor ~2–3).

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Thermal Emission Imaging System (THEMIS) observations used to obtain MY36 airborne dust climatology for PCM dust scenario reconstruction
datasets.measurement_observable: Airborne dust observations used to reconstruct simulated spatial dust distributions for MY36 in the Mars Planetary Climate Model comparison
datasets.data_type_product_type: Orbital atmospheric observations (used as constraints for dust scenario reconstruction)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Martian Year 36 (used to reconstruct dust scenario representative of Perseverance first Martian year conditions)
datasets.how_used: THEMIS-based atmospheric observations were used (together with MCS) to obtain a MY36 dust climatology that was then used to reconstruct the simulated spatial/vertical dust distributions in the Mars Planetary Climate Model (PCM) runs compared against MEDA water vapor measurements.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Climate Sounder (MCS) observations used to obtain MY36 airborne dust climatology for PCM dust scenario reconstruction
datasets.measurement_observable: Atmospheric dust observations used to reconstruct simulated spatial and vertical dust distributions for MY36 in the Mars Planetary Climate Model comparison
datasets.data_type_product_type: Orbital atmospheric observations (used as constraints for dust scenario reconstruction)
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: Martian Year 36 (used to reconstruct dust scenario representative of Perseverance first Martian year conditions)
datasets.how_used: MCS atmospheric observations were used (together with THEMIS) to derive a MY36 airborne dust climatology that constrained the dust scenario used in Mars Planetary Climate Model (PCM) simulations compared with MEDA observations at Jezero.

output_parsed.paper_title: Present-day thermal and water activity environment of the Mars Sample Return collection

queries.query: I need the full set of in-situ meteorology observations from the Perseverance rover’s Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer at Jezero crater spanning the first Martian year, including relative humidity, pressure, air temperature, and ground brightness temperature, to quantify the diurnal atmospheric–surface water exchange and assess frost-formation conditions.

Retrieve the derived Jezero near-surface water vapor volume mixing ratio and derived surface water activity time series computed from Perseverance MEDA relative humidity and ground temperature measurements, emphasizing nighttime local-time coverage, to evaluate seasonal/diurnal habitability-relevant water availability at the surface.

output_parsed.paper_title: Present-day thermal and water activity environment of the Mars Sample Return collection

queries.query: For Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer daytime (~14 LMST) mapping, compile a seasonal climatology of atmospheric water vapor total column (precipitable microns) for the northern mid-latitudes encompassing the Jezero crater region, using zonal averages and solar-longitude binning to characterize interannual variability across Mars Years 24–27.

Using Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer derived products, extract gridded total-column H2O abundance (precipitable microns) on the standard coarse latitude/longitude grid with seasonal (solar-longitude) binning for Mars Years 24–27, to quantify regional-to-global gradients in column water vapor relevant to the Jezero crater environment.

final_output.query: I need the full set of in-situ meteorology observations from the Perseverance rover’s Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer at Jezero crater spanning the first Martian year, including relative humidity, pressure, air temperature, and ground brightness temperature, to quantify the diurnal atmospheric–surface water exchange and assess frost-formation conditions.

Retrieve the derived Jezero near-surface water vapor volume mixing ratio and derived surface water activity time series computed from Perseverance MEDA relative humidity and ground temperature measurements, emphasizing nighttime local-time coverage, to evaluate seasonal/diurnal habitability-relevant water availability at the surface.

For Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer daytime (~14 LMST) mapping, compile a seasonal climatology of atmospheric water vapor total column (precipitable microns) for the northern mid-latitudes encompassing the Jezero crater region, using zonal averages and solar-longitude binning to characterize interannual variability across Mars Years 24–27.

Using Mars Global Surveyor Thermal Emission Spectrometer derived products, extract gridded total-column H2O abundance (precipitable microns) on the standard coarse latitude/longitude grid with seasonal (solar-longitude) binning for Mars Years 24–27, to quantify regional-to-global gradients in column water vapor relevant to the Jezero crater environment.

Compile Mars Odyssey THEMIS orbital observations of atmospheric dust acquired during Martian Year 36 to generate a seasonally resolved, planet-wide dust loading climatology suitable for prescribing the dust scenario in Mars general circulation model simulations.

Use Mars Odyssey THEMIS atmospheric dust observations from Martian Year 36 to constrain the timing and relative intensity of major dust events for reconstructing the spatial and vertical dust distributions used in Mars Planetary Climate Model sensitivity studies.

Assemble Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Climate Sounder derived atmospheric dust profile products spanning Martian Year 36 to construct a vertically resolved airborne dust climatology suitable for constraining dust scenario forcing in Mars Planetary Climate Model simulations of present-day Jezero conditions.

Use Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Climate Sounder raw limb-viewing observations acquired during Martian Year 36 to independently retrieve atmospheric dust loading and vertical structure, and to cross-check the airborne dust climatology adopted for climate-model comparisons at Jezero crater.
